lessons.title: A good book
lessons.goal: I can talk about a good book.

newItems.definition: the events in a story
the good main person in a story
a short story with animals that teaches something
to read a book to the end
the book I like the most

lessons.mainWordForms: Plot is a noun. Plot means the events in a story. The plot is good.
lessons.use: Use this when you talk about a good book.
lessons.expressionTask: Tom and Lily talk about a good book. What do they say?
lessons.grammar: past simple for finished stories: I finished the book yesterday
context: Tom and Lily talk about a good book.
Tom says, 'I finished the book yesterday. My favorite book is a fable. The hero is brave and kind.'
dialogue: Lily, what is a plot?
It is the events in a story. The plot is good.
Who is the hero?
He is the good main person in the story. The hero is brave.
Do you finish a book every week?
Yes. I finish a book every week. My favorite book is a fable.
lessons.listening: Tom and Lily talk about a good book. Tom says, 'I finished the book yesterday. My favorite book is a fable. The hero is brave and kind.' Lily says, 'What is a plot?' Tom says, 'It is the events in a story. The plot is good.'
lessons.question: What did Tom finish yesterday?
lessons.reading: On Monday, Tom and Lily talk about a good book. Tom says, 'I finished the book yesterday. I finish a book every week. I read my favorite book every day. The plot is good. The hero is brave and kind. I like the hero very much.' Lily says, 'What is a plot?' Tom says, 'It is the events in a story. The plot is good. A plot can be funny or sad. I like a good plot.' Lily says, 'What is a fable?' Tom says, 'It is a short story with animals that teaches something. A fable is fun to read. I read a fable with my friends. We finish a book every week. My favorite book is a fable about a hero. I like books very much.'
lessons.speaking: Tell a friend about a good book. What do you say?
lessons.speakingSample: I talk about a good book with my friend Tom. I finished the book yesterday. I finish a book every week. I read my favorite book every day. The plot is good. The hero is brave and kind. I like the hero very much. We read a fable with our friends.
lessons.writing: Write a short email to a friend about a good book. Say what you do.
lessons.writingSample: Dear Anna, I want to tell you about a good book. I finished the book yesterday. I finish a book every week. I read my favorite book every day. The plot is good. The hero is brave and kind. I like the hero very much. We read a fable with our friends. A good book is fun for all of us. See you soon. Best, Lily
lessons.sound: Plot has its strongest beat on PLOT. In plot, say PLOT clearly at the start. In hero, say HEER clearly at the start.

lessons.title: Bedtime stories
lessons.goal: I can talk about bedtime stories.

newItems.definition: the person who tells a story
a story
a story you read before bed
to move to the next page of a book
the last page of a book

mainWord.definition: the person who tells a story

lessons.mainWordForms: Narrator is a noun. Narrator means the person who tells a story. She is the narrator.
lessons.expression: I was reading a bedtime story.
lessons.use: Use this when you talk about bedtime stories.
lessons.expressionTask: Tom and Lily talk about bedtime stories. What do they say?
lessons.grammar: past continuous for scenes: I was reading a bedtime story
lessons.pattern: I was reading a bedtime story.
lessons.example: I was reading a bedtime story.
context: Tom and Lily talk about bedtime stories.
Tom says, 'I was reading a bedtime story. The narrator tells a good tale.'
dialogue: Lily, what is a narrator?
It is the person who tells a story. She is the narrator.
What is a tale?
It is a story. I like this tale.
Do you turn the page at night?
Yes. I turn the page and read the last page.
lessons.listening: Tom and Lily talk about bedtime stories. Tom says, 'I was reading a bedtime story. The narrator tells a good tale.' Lily says, 'What is a narrator?' Tom says, 'It is the person who tells a story.' Lily says, 'What is a tale?' Tom says, 'It is a story. I like this tale very much.'
lessons.question: What was Tom reading?
lessons.reading: On Tuesday, Tom and Lily talk about bedtime stories. Tom says, 'I was reading a bedtime story. The narrator tells a good tale. I like this tale very much. I turn the page and read the last page. A bedtime story is fun at night.' Lily says, 'What is a narrator?' Tom says, 'It is the person who tells a story. She is the narrator. A narrator can tell a good tale.' Lily says, 'What is a tale?' Tom says, 'It is a story. I like this tale. I read a bedtime story with my friends. We turn the page every night. I read the last page at home. Bedtime stories are good for all of us.'
lessons.speaking: Tell a friend about bedtime stories. What do you say?
lessons.speakingSample: I talk about bedtime stories with my friend Tom. I was reading a bedtime story. The narrator tells a good tale. I like this tale very much. I turn the page and read the last page. A bedtime story is fun at night. We read a bedtime story with our friends.
lessons.writing: Write a short email to a friend about bedtime stories. Say what you do.
lessons.writingSample: Dear Anna, I want to tell you about bedtime stories. I was reading a bedtime story. The narrator tells a good tale. I like this tale very much. I turn the page and read the last page. A bedtime story is fun at night. We read a bedtime story with our friends. Bedtime stories are good for all of us. See you soon. Best, Lily
lessons.sound: Narrator has its strongest beat on NARR. In narrator, say NARR clearly at the start. In tale, say TALE clearly.
lessons.wordSample: The person who tells a story.

lessons.title: A mysterious tale
lessons.goal: I can talk about a mysterious tale.

newItems.definition: the bad person in a story
strange and hard to understand
with magic
a story about love
to live a happy life after the story ends

mainWord.definition: the bad person in a story

lessons.mainWordForms: Villain is a noun. Villain means the bad person in a story. He is the villain.
lessons.expression: I was reading when she came in.
lessons.use: Use this when you talk about a mysterious tale.
lessons.expressionTask: Tom and Lily talk about a mysterious tale. What do they say?
lessons.grammar: past simple and past continuous: I was reading when she came in
lessons.pattern: I was reading when she came in.
lessons.task: I was reading when she ___ in.
lessons.example: I was reading when she came in.
context: Tom and Lily talk about a mysterious tale.
Tom says, 'I was reading when she came in. It is a love story. They live happily ever after.'
dialogue: Lily, what is a villain?
It is the bad person in a story. He is the villain.
What does mysterious mean?
It means strange and hard to understand. The tale is mysterious.
Is it a love story?
Yes. It is a love story. They live happily ever after.
lessons.listening: Tom and Lily talk about a mysterious tale. Tom says, 'I was reading when she came in. It is a love story.' Lily says, 'What is a villain?' Tom says, 'It is the bad person in a story.' Lily says, 'What does mysterious mean?' Tom says, 'It means strange and hard to understand.'
lessons.question: What kind of story is it?
lessons.reading: On Wednesday, Tom and Lily talk about a mysterious tale. Tom says, 'I was reading when she came in. It is a love story. The villain is bad, but the hero is good. The tale is mysterious and magical. They live happily ever after.' Lily says, 'What is a villain?' Tom says, 'It is the bad person in a story. He is the villain. A villain can be very bad.' Lily says, 'What does mysterious mean?' Tom says, 'It means strange and hard to understand. The tale is mysterious. It is magical too. I like a love story with our friends. They live happily ever after at home. A love story is fun to read.'
lessons.readingQ: What kind of story is it?
lessons.speaking: Tell a friend about a mysterious tale. What do you say?
lessons.speakingSample: I talk about a mysterious tale with my friend Tom. I was reading when she came in. It is a love story. The villain is bad, but the hero is good. The tale is mysterious and magical. They live happily ever after. I like a love story with our friends very much.
lessons.writing: Write a short email to a friend about a mysterious tale. Say what you think.
lessons.writingSample: Dear Anna, I want to tell you about a mysterious tale. I was reading when she came in. It is a love story. The villain is bad, but the hero is good. The tale is mysterious and magical. They live happily ever after. I like a love story with our friends very much. A love story is fun for all of us. See you soon. Best, Lily
lessons.sound: Villain has its strongest beat on VILL. In villain, say VILL clearly at the start. In mysterious, say MYST clearly at the start.
lessons.wordSample: The bad person in a story.

lessons.title: The hero of the story
lessons.goal: I can talk about the hero of a story.

newItems.definition: a film or book that comes after another one
a book or film many people love for a long time
the chapter after this one
a group of people who read the same book
the most important idea

mainWord.definition: a film or book that comes after another one

lessons.mainWordForms: Sequel is a noun. Sequel means a film or book that comes after another one. It is a sequel.
lessons.expression: He is the hero who saves the town.
lessons.use: Use this when you talk about the hero of a story.
lessons.expressionTask: Tom and Lily talk about the hero of a story. What do they say?
lessons.grammar: relative clauses with who: He is the hero who saves the town
lessons.pattern: He is the hero who saves the town.
lessons.task: He is the hero who ___ the town.
lessons.example: He is the hero who saves the town.
context: Tom and Lily talk about the hero of a story.
Tom says, 'He is the hero who saves the town. It is a classic. The main idea is good.'
dialogue: Lily, what is a sequel?
It is a film or book that comes after another one. It is a sequel.
What is a classic?
It is a book or film many people love for a long time. It is a classic.
What is the main idea?
It is the most important idea. We read the next chapter in our book club.
lessons.listening: Tom and Lily talk about the hero of a story. Tom says, 'He is the hero who saves the town. It is a classic.' Lily says, 'What is a sequel?' Tom says, 'It is a film or book that comes after another one. It is a sequel.'
lessons.question: Who is the hero?
lessons.correct: The hero who saves the town
lessons.other: The bad person in a story
lessons.reading: On Thursday, Tom and Lily talk about the hero of a story. Tom says, 'He is the hero who saves the town. It is a classic. We read the next chapter in our book club. The main idea is good. It is a sequel.' Lily says, 'What is a sequel?' Tom says, 'It is a film or book that comes after another one. It is a sequel. A sequel can be very good.' Lily says, 'What is a classic?' Tom says, 'It is a book or film many people love for a long time. It is a classic. I like a classic with our friends. We read the next chapter every week. I like a book club at school. The main idea is good for all of us.'
lessons.readingA: The hero who saves the town.
lessons.speaking: Tell a friend about the hero of a story. What do you say?
lessons.speakingSample: I talk about the hero of a story with my friend Tom. He is the hero who saves the town. It is a classic. We read the next chapter in our book club. The main idea is good. It is a sequel. I like a classic with our friends very much.
lessons.writing: Write a short email to a friend about the hero of a story. Say what you think.
lessons.writingSample: Dear Anna, I want to tell you about the hero of a story. He is the hero who saves the town. It is a classic. We read the next chapter in our book club. The main idea is good. It is a sequel. I like a classic with our friends very much. A classic is fun for all of us. See you soon. Best, Lily
lessons.sound: Sequel has its strongest beat on SEE. In sequel, say SEE clearly at the start. In classic, say CLASS clearly at the start.
lessons.wordSample: A film or book that comes after another one.

lessons.title: Books about real people
lessons.goal: I can talk about books about real people.

newItems.definition: a person who writes poems
a short piece of writing with short lines
poems
a film or book that comes from a real story
newItems.example: It is based on a true story.

newItems.definition: the last part of a story
newItems.example: It is the end of the story.

lessons.mainWordForms: Poet is a noun. Poet means a person who writes poems. She is a poet.
lessons.expression: It is the book that I like best.
lessons.use: Use this when you talk about books about real people.
lessons.expressionTask: Tom and Lily talk about books about real people. What do they say?
lessons.grammar: relative clauses with which and that: It is the book that I like best
lessons.pattern: It is the book that I like best.
lessons.task: It is the book ___ I like best.
lessons.example: It is the book that I like best.
context: Tom and Lily talk about books about real people.
Tom says, 'It is the book that I like best. It is based on a true story. The end of the story is good.'
dialogue: Lily, what is a poet?
It is a person who writes poems. She is a poet.
What is a poem?
It is a short piece of writing with short lines. I like this poem.
Do you like poetry?
Yes. I like poetry. It is based on a true story.
lessons.listening: Tom and Lily talk about books about real people. Tom says, 'It is the book that I like. It is based on a true story.' Lily says, 'What is a poet?' Tom says, 'It is a person who writes poems.' Lily says, 'What is a poem?' Tom says, 'It is a short piece of writing.'
lessons.question: What does Tom like?
lessons.reading: On Friday, Tom and Lily talk about books about real people. Tom says, 'It is the book that I like best. It is based on a true story. The end of the story is good. She is a poet. I like her poem very much.' Lily says, 'What is a poet?' Tom says, 'It is a person who writes poems. She is a poet. A poet can write a good poem.' Lily says, 'What is a poem?' Tom says, 'It is a short piece of writing with short lines. I like this poem. I like poetry with our friends. We read a poem every day. It is based on a true story. The end of the story is good for all of us.'
lessons.speaking: Tell a friend about books about real people. What do you say?
lessons.speakingSample: I talk about books about real people with my friend Tom. It is the book that I like best. It is based on a true story. The end of the story is good. She is a poet. I like her poem very much. I like poetry with our friends today.
lessons.writing: Write a short email to a friend about books about real people. Say what you think.
lessons.writingSample: Dear Anna, I want to tell you about books about real people. It is the book that I like best. It is based on a true story. The end of the story is good. She is a poet. I like her poem very much. I like poetry with our friends today. Books about real people are good for all of us. See you soon. Best, Lily
lessons.sound: Poet has its strongest beat on PO. In poet, say PO clearly at the start. In poem, say PO clearly at the start.

lessons.title: A film at the movies
lessons.goal: I can talk about a film at the movies.

newItems.definition: the person who tells actors what to do
the words of a film or play
at the place where you watch films
a film that tells about something
newItems.example: It is a film about a king.

newItems.definition: used to say what a film tells about
newItems.example: The film is about a king.

mainWord.definition: the person who tells actors what to do

lessons.mainWordForms: Director is a noun. Director means the person who tells actors what to do. She is the director.
lessons.expression: The film was funny and exciting.
lessons.use: Use this when you talk about a film at the movies.
lessons.expressionTask: Tom and Lily talk about a film at the movies. What do they say?
lessons.grammar: adjectives for describing stories: The film was funny and exciting
lessons.pattern: The film was funny and exciting.
lessons.example: The film was funny and exciting.
context: Tom and Lily talk about a film at the movies.
Tom says, 'The film was funny and exciting. The film is about a king. We are at the movies.'
dialogue: Lily, what is a director?
It is the person who tells actors what to do. She is the director.
What is a script?
It is the words of a film or play. I read the script.
Is the film about a king?
Yes. The film is about a king. We are at the movies.
lessons.listening: Tom and Lily talk about a film at the movies. Tom says, 'The film was funny and exciting. The film is about a king.' Lily says, 'What is a director?' Tom says, 'It is the person who tells actors what to do.' Lily says, 'What is a script?' Tom says, 'It is the words.'
lessons.question: What is the film about?
lessons.reading: On Saturday, Tom and Lily talk about a film at the movies. Tom says, 'The film was funny and exciting. The film is about a king. We are at the movies. She is the director. I read the script.' Lily says, 'What is a director?' Tom says, 'It is the person who tells actors what to do. She is the director. A director can make a good film.' Lily says, 'What is a script?' Tom says, 'It is the words of a film or play. I read the script. I like a film about a king. The film is about a king who is good. We are at the movies with our friends.'
lessons.speaking: Tell a friend about a film at the movies. What do you say?
lessons.speakingSample: I talk about a film at the movies with my friend Tom. The film was funny and exciting. The film is about a king. We are at the movies. She is the director. I read the script. I like a film about a king very much. We are at the movies with our friends.
lessons.writing: Write a short email to a friend about a film at the movies. Say what you think.
lessons.writingSample: Dear Anna, I want to tell you about a film at the movies. The film was funny and exciting. The film is about a king. We are at the movies. She is the director. I read the script. I like a film about a king very much. We are at the movies with our friends. A film is fun for all of us. See you soon. Best, Lily
lessons.sound: Director has its strongest beat on RECT. In director, say RECT clearly in the middle. In script, say SCRIPT clearly.
lessons.wordSample: The person who tells actors what to do.

lessons.title: What did she say?
lessons.goal: I can say what people said about a film.

newItems.definition: a person who finds out who did a crime
a small thing that helps you find an answer
a love story
used to say a book is very good
used to say a film was very good

mainWord.definition: a person who finds out who did a crime

lessons.mainWordForms: Detective is a noun. Detective means a person who finds out who did a crime. She is a detective.
lessons.expression: She said that the film was great.
lessons.use: Use this when you say what people said about a film.
lessons.expressionTask: Tom and Lily talk about what people said. What do they say?
lessons.grammar: reported speech basics: She said that the film was great
lessons.pattern: She said that the film was great.
lessons.task: She said that the film was ___.
lessons.example: She said that the film was great.
context: Tom and Lily talk about what people said.
Tom says, 'She said that the film was great. I can't put it down. It is a romance.'
dialogue: Lily, what is a detective?
It is a person who finds out who did a crime. She is a detective.
What is a clue?
It is a small thing that helps you find an answer. I find a clue.
Can you put the book down?
No. I can't put it down. The film was great.
lessons.listening: Tom and Lily talk about what people said. Tom says, 'She said that the film was great. I can't put it down.' Lily says, 'What is a detective?' Tom says, 'It is a person who finds out who did a crime.' Lily says, 'What is a clue?' Tom says, 'It is a small thing.'
lessons.question: What did she say?
lessons.reading: On Sunday, Tom and Lily talk about what people said. Tom says, 'She said that the film was great. I can't put it down. It is a romance. She is a detective. I find a clue.' Lily says, 'What is a detective?' Tom says, 'It is a person who finds out who did a crime. She is a detective. A detective can find a clue.' Lily says, 'What is a clue?' Tom says, 'It is a small thing that helps you find an answer. I find a clue every day. I can't put it down. The film was great. I like it very much. It is a romance for all of us.'
lessons.speaking: Tell a friend what people said about a film. What do you say?
lessons.speakingSample: I talk about what people said with my friend Tom. She said that the film was great. I can't put it down. It is a romance. She is a detective. I find a clue every day. I like it very much. We talk about the film with our friends every day.
lessons.writing: Write a short email to a friend about what people said. Say what they said.
lessons.writingSample: Dear Anna, I want to tell you what people said about the film. She said that the film was great. I can't put it down. It is a romance. She is a detective. I find a clue every day. I like it very much. We talk about the film with our friends every day. What people say is fun for all of us. See you soon. Best, Lily
lessons.sound: Detective has its strongest beat on TECT. In detective, say TECT clearly in the middle. In clue, say CLUE clearly.
lessons.wordSample: A person who finds out who did a crime.

lessons.title: Use story English in a new situation
lessons.goal: I can use story English in a new situation.

newItems.definition: a story about magic and imaginary worlds
the son of a king or queen
an ending where people are sad
to be a person in a play or film
used to say a book was very good

mainWord.definition: a story about magic and imaginary worlds

lessons.mainWordForms: Fantasy is a noun. Fantasy means a story about magic and imaginary worlds. It is a fantasy.
lessons.expression: I can use story English in a new situation.
lessons.use: Use this when you talk about using English in a new place.
lessons.expressionTask: Emma talks about story English. What does she say?
lessons.pattern: I can use story English in a new situation.
lessons.task: I can use story English in a new ___.
lessons.example: I can use story English in a new situation.
context: Emma talks about story English with her mother.
Emma says, 'I can use story English in a new situation. The book was great. I play a part in the play.'
dialogue: Emma, what is a fantasy?
It is a story about magic and imaginary worlds. It is a fantasy.
Who is a prince?
He is the son of a king or queen. He is a prince.
Is it a sad ending?
No. It is a happy ending. The book was great.
lessons.listening: Emma talks about story English. Emma says, 'I can use story English in a new situation. The book was great.' Her mother says, 'What is a fantasy?' Emma says, 'It is a story about magic.' Her mother says, 'Who is a prince?' Emma says, 'He is the son of a king.'
lessons.question: What is a fantasy?
lessons.reading: On Monday, Emma talks about story English with her mother. Emma says, 'I can use story English in a new situation. The book was great. It is a fantasy. He is a prince. I play a part in the play.' Her mother says, 'What is a fantasy?' Emma says, 'It is a story about magic and imaginary worlds. It is a fantasy. A fantasy is fun to read.' Her mother says, 'Who is a prince?' Emma says, 'He is the son of a king or queen. He is a prince. It is a sad ending, but the book was great. I play a part in the play every week. I use story English every day.'
lessons.readingA: A story about magic and imaginary worlds.
lessons.speaking: Tell a friend about story English. What do you say?
lessons.speakingSample: I talk about story English with my friend Emma. I can use story English in a new situation. The book was great. It is a fantasy. He is a prince. I play a part in the play. It is a sad ending, but I like story English very much today.
lessons.writing: Write a short email to a friend about story English. Say what story English means to you.
lessons.writingSample: Dear Anna, I want to tell you about story English. I can use story English in a new situation. The book was great. It is a fantasy. He is a prince. I play a part in the play. It is a sad ending, but I like story English very much today. Today I can use it in a new place. Story English is good for all of us. See you soon. Best, Emma
lessons.sound: Fantasy has its strongest beat on FANT. In fantasy, say FANT clearly at the start. In prince, say PRINCE clearly.
lessons.wordSample: A story about magic and imaginary worlds.
